Definition: from G1487 and G5100; if any:--he that, if a(-ny) man('s thing, from any, ought), whether any, whosoever.
BiblicalUsage: This phrase means if any or if anyone, and it opens the door to whoever will listen. Jesus says, If any man have ears to hear, let him hear, Paul says the commandments are summed up in loving your neighbour, and he warns that if any man defiles the temple of God, God will destroy him. The phrase is wide open, and it includes me.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe if any means the invitation and the warning are both for everyone, because no one is left out of either.
RelatedTopics: Obedience; Fear of the Lord; Faith
